评论更新&终评： 游戏表面看似乎应该推荐大于不推荐。但这游戏玩上几个小时会发现其实并不如意。 不是不好玩，是设定层面的局限，也是韩式游戏的局限。 首先 角色之间的开荒能力差距太大，这就说明了数据性的根本问题。 其次 每个章节内难度浮动都是较大的， 总共十几分钟的过图时间，居然能体验到从割草，到打不动的难度，怎么制作出来的？ 再次 游戏本质上是极端卡数值的，过每个章节 你只有一个条件，就能能对这个章节内头目，首领割草，做不到轻松推倒，那就基本过不了，因此明明是只要十几分钟过图，但实际每一个章节，你得打上几个小时来累计资源解锁局外，升级武器等等。 最后 糟糕的刷宝体验，这游戏的刷宝体验等于没有，别看出去一趟满背包的东西，但是能用的基本没有。只能赌运气等出个好的高伤武器。 游戏总体战斗体验还行， 但是作为一个数据结构化的游戏， 游戏在数据面上呈现 杂乱，无效，压制等多个方面的问题。 换句话说 进度的平衡性 与人物之间的平衡性 非常糟糕，

即使是*管也会有贤者时间，但这个游戏爽完接着还是爽

[h1]时间紧，任务重，给我个30秒，我还能再顺带解救世界[/h1] [quote] [h2]当其他类幸存者游戏还在研究“怎么活下来”时，《零秒：时光的归途》已经逼着你去思考“怎么才能跑得更快”。[/h2] [/quote] 本作以类幸存者玩法作为操作框架，然后又在此的基础上还另外引入了一个颠覆性的时间倒计数机制，玩家会被要求在[b]30秒钟内直接通关连续一整场的战斗[/b]，事实上这本身就是一个不太可能的事情，基于此所以游戏引入了时停这一机制，于是，一场与时间竞速并回溯到过去拯救世界的玩法就此展开。 简单来说，这个所谓的30秒其实只是一个幌子，当击败BOSS、或者完成挑战房间里的挑战后就可以延长30秒的倒计时、而中途拾取到的对应肉鸽三选一增益，也有一部分会影响时间的流动的构筑存在。游戏这样设计除去契合剧情以外，其主要的目是还为了鼓励玩家在游戏中快速决策，主动去寻找BOSS击杀，而不是保守地待着一个地方练级。玩的时候不妨将倒计时当成另一种资源，玩的时候也就没那么有紧迫感了。 游戏最大一特色还当属于，有着极其强烈的反馈体验了，从养成性上来说，是玩家一开始的人物面板的属性值从零到有构筑，主基地随着后续冒险的深入探索，使得功能逐一解禁，看着人物基地越来越大，天赋树点的越来越满，可以说这就是极其正向的正反馈，此外基本做到了每次出门打怪都能收获满满的回家，游戏的节奏性这点给予好评。 从对局中来说，作为一款类幸存者游戏而言，游戏的挑战设计是基于[b]等级数值膨胀[/b]建立的，游戏中玩家角色的等级数值增长的非常快，它要求玩家按照地图中划分对应的等级区间去进行练级与挑战，当够格（等级足够）时，即可奔向下一个房间进行挑战。 只要你角色当前的等级不够高时，直接闯进还立即对玩家进行提示，此时基本不足以对本场房间战斗的小怪造成伤害，可以说打不过那就是打不过，却没办法像一般的动作类RPG那样依靠自己游戏理解与技术来智胜过关，你能够做到最好的地方，无非就是靠点战斗间隙进行的小走位，还有及时反应来规避少吃点伤害仅此而已。 但你要说这完全是缺点嘛，我个人又觉得倒也不算完全是，你可以代入这么一个视角：看着游戏里角色，从第一个房间开始起的[b]0级[/b]，再到后面关卡的[b]上10w+[/b]，后期地图随手攻击一下就是跳动上百万的金色伤害数字，可以说这个数值的膨胀的看着还是很带感的，颇有那么点增量游戏的味道。 《零秒》这个游戏总体玩下来的感受就是：基本不需要动啥脑子，开着时停只管呼呼一顿猛冲，沿途的BOSS见到就刷，见到了好的装备及时换，及时冲刺躲掉BOSS红色攻击区域就行。可以说在幸存者前人的基础上，也很好的彰显自己的游戏特色，各种肉鸽局内构筑词条足够丰富，系统设计上都有老道且成熟的表现。 但我个人还是喜欢玩那种与交互性比较强的游戏，在如今这个同质化游戏频繁昙花一现的年代，还是更加想看到那些敢于去大胆创新玩法的游戏，而《零秒》这个游戏没有固步自封，做到了自己对于游戏见解里的那份创新，这就已经足够了。 [h2]官方B站就有号，今年深圳核聚变曾参展，游戏定价良心，画风与场景表现力优秀，首发八折仅38.4，可以交个朋友。[/h2] [quote]关注[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/36224058/]老实人鉴赏家 [/url] [url=https://steamcommunity.com/groups/laoshirenLSR]老实人评测[/url]：独立游戏爱好者聚集地，黄油绅士交流中心。 不错过游戏的亮点，不放过游戏的槽点，带给玩家最直观的测评感受。[/quote]

......这是我玩过最不爽的肉鸽了。 它并不局限于肉鸽那种一局只要花时间或者操作技术力和得到随机强化就能得到不俗的成长数值和其他可视性加成。 而是将重心放在局外的成长上，得到一种刷宝+搜打撤的一种很新奇的肉鸽。 优点就是如此。 但是缺点就是，玩了两小时我确实得不到什么很爽的正反馈， 反而觉得局外的养成有点令人头疼，可装备的背包格子要肝，局外天赋要肝，开局强化要肝，局内带出来的一次性物品转为永久也要肝。 关键是肝出来的强化也没什么用，开了一把新的局内感受不到多少的成长，数值高的怪打你照样是高数值的伤害。 没有强力的刷宝，也没有搜打撤的刺激，肉鸽的强力加成也没有，能看到的是局外的数值大大影响局内强度的结果。别的肉鸽里货币强化也没什么稀有度，在这里货币强化居然能上到紫色这种稀有度。隔壁梦之形局外都没这么肝，至少没有一些局外我也能打完一整局。 目前的我是真的玩不懂的。
这个时间，怎么花不完！

看到更新了1.0.6的版本 并且更新报告里有提到【修复了在某些情况下，游戏可能会在特定首领战期间或结束后立即崩溃的问题】 打了两把 第一把正常通关 第二把在第四关最终BOSS没变人的1形态下 使用装置+化身技的连协秒杀后再次闪退 我的评价是依然不能玩 气死我了 ================ 第一次评测后2小时追加评论 气笑了 又打了一把 这次是最终BOSS打完 依旧捡不了掉落物 然后在最后结算画面抽奖抽完点击确认的时候闪退 启动游戏后数据回到了打完图3下水道进入图4前 图4刷的掉落物又没了 ================ 思考了一下，以小品类幸存者rouge来说局内的成就感不错，局外成长也不抠搜，但目前的一些恶性BUG只能给个中评以下的程度，之后修复了这些问题会修复评价。 首先聊聊几个恶性BUG 1.我在总第3把还是第4把就干掉了普通结局的最终BOSS，在剧情过完后游戏直接闪退，我参考了评论区，发现并不是个例。 并且在我再次进入游戏后发现身上的物品只保留了到了图2的数据，下水道和最后一图的都没了，刷装备主要就是最后2图，导致挫败感非常强烈。 2.之后我再次通关了一次，本次正常过完了结局剧情，也跳了成就，然后就直接跳结算了，BOSS的掉落物全在地上并没有任何时间捡，因为在杀完BOSS的瞬间就直接进入剧情然后结算了。 3.在这之后游戏提示我可以解锁多次元模式了，游戏指南说是在时光机里，但我并没有看到解锁，我去时光机管理那拉满了一半的选项，时光机依然没有，直到我又经行了两局游戏，完成了一些游戏内的任务才在时光机内看到多次元模式的选项。 4.某些任务的奖励是在游戏局内完成后即时结算的，会在当前地图的随机一个点自动刷出，如果位置不好，就会把装备卡在地形对面，只能瞪眼看着。 同理，比如图2与图3的最终BOSS 打死后掉落物会和传送门完全重合，特别是图3，不知道是BOSS的尸体有碰撞还是BOSS身下有个地形，导致掉落物非常难以拾取，一不小心就直接进了传送门。 然后聊几个待优化，对于这类做BD的数值肉鸽游戏来说非常不人性化的地方 1.没有最终数值面板 局内只有3个面板 面板1是基础属性 显示攻击 防御 生命 敏捷 幸运 面板2是游戏所谓的详细能力值 显示了局内能获得的各种加成 面板3是BUFF面板 而最关键的结果数据没有 也就是说 我只能看到我的攻击速度加成是XX% 我的暴击率加成是YY% 我的某某伤害加成是ZZ% 但我无法直观看到我当前的攻击速度是每秒多少 我的暴击率最终是多少 有没有超出边际效益 我的武器最终的输出到底怎么样 这就导致在BD的时候非常难受 在数值差距不是很夸张的时候根本不知道更换某件装备后到底是更强还是更弱了 2.非常奇怪的DPS统计 游戏局内有相当多的伤害来源 比如天赋联动 比如DEBUFF 比如武器栏特效 但局内只在左侧给了1个当前武器的DPS，这就导致各种非武器伤害BD在测试最终DPS的时候非常困难 最简单的比方就是如果我用樱花武士来做一套流血debuff的BD，在我目前的进度能看到两个引爆的办法，分别是天赋里化身技引爆流血层数和武器强化里的武器攻击引爆流血层数造成爆炸伤害。 但我根本无法测试其他提高流血伤害的天赋是否对这两种方式的最终伤害有加成。 说到这了，顺便一说，家里那个假人也很不知所谓。 BD的大头在局内天赋和武器强化，但家里的假人只能测纯装备效果，我从没见过这样的假人... 3.各个不同的武器的攻击范围完全没有显示，明明在选定武器的时候很简单的在脚下显示一个圈，就像樱花忍者的化身天赋的结界那样就行的 而且游戏里甚至有范围的度量衡——px 但就是不告诉你具体是多少 希望能尽快更新修复吧…… 评价于2026.07.14 游戏版本：ver.1.0.5.0

Calling this game "1.0" has to be a scam. Underdeveloped mechanics, missing avatars, and fewer items and skills than an alpha/prototype you can find on itch, combined with a storyline that is also unfinished and has no ending -- if this is what is 1.0 these days, then we are all collectively screwed. Don't buy this. Let it rot. EDIT: I feel like I gave the game an unfair review, just throwing out buzz words like regurgitated online news outlets. I will go into detail about what I find this game is missing. Most reviews that talk about the game have between 2-8 hours, which is, frankly, not enough to even clear the game once and unlock multidimensional stuff. I have played the game a lot, and I had fun until the multidimensional stuff. Let's begin with the "underdeveloped mechanics". Bleed is the only status effect that is actually supported by skills and items. I don't believe I have ever seen an item that gives you more poison damage, or even burn damage for that matter. There are avatars that utilize those as the "core" of their strategy, so it's not like the devs forgot about it, but the items do not exist (with some technical exceptions). I do have faith that the developers will eventually add support for them, but my annoyance, at the time, was calling this "1.0" AKA "full release, no obligation to continue updating, the game is finished" is a bit wild. It's like buying a car with no wheels. You are going to get the wheels, eventually, because that's common sense, but you are buying a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ car that was built in a factory, it should come with wheels. There is also the obvious fact that like half the avatar pedestals do not have a corresponding avatar to go on them. They clearly exist to have an avatar on them, but there is no avatar. This either tells me there is planned DLC, or the "1.0" claim is a complete fabrication. I don't like either of these possibilities. The game has 30 items per category, of which 20 are completely irrelevant. When you do the math, that means this game has about 10 sets total or thereabouts. More than that, every item you get later in the game is more and more disappointing. You are expecting -- hoping for -- an actual upgrade to your arsenal, but you get some bs item that just gives +10% damage taken on hit. When you already have +600%. It is a very, very uninspiring game, and most of your power comes simply from the raw stats. All in all, this game felt more like a very long demo than anything else, and it isn't helped by the unfinished storyline that just... "we will keep fighting and fighting forever and ever." The game is fun, but it doesn't give you a reward for the time you put in. It doesn't meet your expectations, and instead you are left with a worse version of Half Minute Hero, or Inflation RPG, and thinking how much more you'd prefer to play those games instead.

I had to drop Ascent to Zero. It falls into the exact same trap as every other game built on that modern Korean design philosophy: gorgeous to look at, absolutely hollow to play. Once you look past the insane particle effects and shiny character models, you realize there’s zero mechanical substance holding it together. It’s basically an interactive screensaver.

I enjoyed my time with this game, but the demo is highly misleading about what the endgame is actually like. The time stop mechanic is really cool, and it's absolutely necessary to survive against several of the bosses throughout the game, which is why it's so wild to me that Chapter 3 basically gets rid of it. The common enemies in Chapter 3 will still move even when time stop is activated, and if they hit you, you lose 10 seconds. I've been playing a melee build, which is heavily punished in the final chapter. About 50% of the bosses in Chapter 3 also just ignore your time stop ability altogether. It's wild to me that so much of this game is built around this one ability, only for it to become useless for the last third of the game. I genuinely feel rug-pulled. I'm sure that if I grinded for another 10 hours, I could one-shot all the enemies and finish the game, but honestly, I'm not having fun anymore. I wish I could recommend this game, but honestly, play the demo. Where the demo ends is also where the good content, and the fun I was having with this game ended.

首先，游戏的优点是真的非常明确，因为它既不存在属性加点，技能（装置技能）也只有两个，由局外手动选择（可选项会随游戏进度推进逐渐解锁）+局内随机掉落（但是因为池子比较小，所以也不怎么随机）组成，技能树（能力值强化）更是攒够货币无脑点满就行，需要玩家花心思手动进行搭配的实际只有身上的17件装备。 而在装备属性及词条设计上，制作组也是做了相当程度的减法，即同种装备只在品质（在基础数值的基础上提供一定加成，强化装备时也能获得加成）和可选词条上存在分歧，且装备的品质与词条都可以通过消耗“零单元”进行重置，换言之，在配装方面，游戏基本上不存在什么理解门槛，只要能看懂汉字和数字就能按照自身需求轻松搭配，玩起来并不需要费太多脑子，还是挺适合我这种偶尔就想玩玩刷刷刷爽游戏的纯莽系玩家的。（不过在斟酌到底要用某个套装中的哪一件的时候该纠结还是会纠结的…） （友情提示1：随最大等级提升，玩家可以消耗“零单元”在入口处的“命运编辑器”购买自动分解，这样100个背包格子就不会不够用了） （友情提示2：成功率95%+不等于绝对能成功…别问我怎么知道的） 其次，就算抛开技能树，游戏中可以靠游戏推进与局外成长获取的各类加成也是真的多，比如可以增幅各项属性或延长游戏时间的魔方（可惜是一次性的，后期我就懒得拿了），经由图鉴完成率解锁的各项永久加成（看起来很有诱惑力，但补图鉴又实在是太肝了…什么叫想打成就我就得刷满6个职业的专有技术芯片啊？），还有可以消耗等级上限解锁，并在开局前消耗货币购买的时光机加成（普通模式消耗零秒币，多次元模式消耗零单元），总之确实能做到越打越强，越玩越爽。 首先，游戏中的时间可以看作是独立于角色生命值的另一种权重更高的生命值，即，因生命值导致的角色死亡并不是真正的死亡（但是会罚时），游戏只会在时间完全结束后才会迎来结束，算是在某种程度上降低了角色死亡可能带来的负反馈，也在某种程度上提升了游戏的紧张感，决定了玩法的整体思路（即提升攻击力，用尽可能少的时间解决战斗，并尽最大可能提升时间上限）。 不过，话虽是这么说，这个时间实际只有在游戏前期或是BD没有完全成型的情况下才会格外捉襟见肘，毕竟BD成型之后不是我秒Boss就是Boss秒我，根本不存在搞什么左右腾挪的刮痧拉锯战的机会（ 而时停则是非常完美地诠释了它的字面意思，只要启动就能做到彻彻底底的时间停止（但角色和蓝标故障怪不受影响），虽然在时停的过程中武器并不会继续触发攻击[b]（但武器箱中能拿到时停后继续攻击一段时间的武器词条）[/b]，玩家可以在时停的过程中将角色移动到敌人的攻击范围外（时停会一直持续到玩家下一次按下时停键），也可以拿来赶路，还可以拿来在基地的老虎机上作弊（游戏机制确实是这么设计的），总之非常好用。 As time goes on, you can also upgrade the time machine in various ways to get significant bonuses, as well as you are rewarded for trying out every item at least once in passive rewards from a database collection individual. [h2] 30秒通关一个游戏[/h2] 在时间中赛跑，感受战斗的速度与激情。《零秒：时光的归途》是一款十分特别的像素风游戏，其中融合了大量养成升级以及肉鸽强化，让玩家自由地构筑出专属的流派。故事讲述了玩家成为了世界毁灭后唯一幸存下的人类，尝试通过时间倒流救出一起并肩作战的亲人与朋友，现在就让我们一起来看看吧。 [h2] 砸瓦鲁多[/h2] 如果说单纯凭借这回溯的三十秒，让我们去完成拯救同伴击杀最终BOSS，这肯定是一件无法完成的事情。但是时停机制的出现，让一切拥有了可能，除了击杀精英能补充时间等有限手段，基本上我们很多的时候都将保持在时间静止的状态。 在这时我们可以无限使用闪现位移，化身为一道流光穿梭在场地之中。特别是在boss战的环节下这种感觉变得更加强烈，在各种超大范围的攻势下，灵活地进入时停的空间之中，此时还没有完全形成的攻击停止了，四周发射出的弹药也保持不动，我们直接来到攻击死角恢复原样，就能无伤躲过。 但是在这个形态下我们无法进行任何有效的攻击，可能就依靠撞击破坏一下地图中随处可见的圆桶，也正是因为有了这个形态，我们才有了比肩神明的输出。当我们解除时停时，我们的化身就会释放出一次特殊的招式 ，对范围内的敌人造成大量伤害，不同的化身拥有的人物特性不同，所释放的招数也不一样，游戏贴心地将每个化身都打上了对应的标签符号，我们能根据自己的武器装备来选择更加合适的化身。 [h2] 总结[/h2] 对于我个人来说，《零秒：时光的归途》，作为一款时停题材的俯视角动作游戏，各种视觉冲击感拉满的特效，肉鸽芯片搭配上不同的武器装备，玩家可以尝试流派之间的差异乐趣，品味自由构筑的魅力。 并且游戏的局外养成系统也设计得十分完美，配合局内的肉鸽强化效果相互产生连携的爆炸效果。每局游玩时长30秒的设定，使得战斗节奏变得更加紧凑，时停的机制凸显出动与静两种截然不同的风格，玩家逐渐沉浸在战斗的快感下无法自拔，期待来自你的30秒体验。 [table][td]欢迎关注鉴赏家[url= https://store.steampowered.com/curator/46072643]“黄油收集师”[/url][/td][/table]

I saw the super slick animation for this and bought it on the hype alone, and when I got in I was pretty put off by the graphics of the actual game. I decided I'd give it a shot anyway and 9 hours later I had not eaten or taken a break to do anything else. This is a good game, and you should buy it right now and start playing. That said- the game does not present itself very well on the store page and you're in for some surprises if you're expecting a Hades style rogue-like (which was what I was expecting going in.) You have 30 seconds to beat a whole level, which sounds insane till you realize you can stop time. No- not bullet time, no- not for a few seconds- you can straight up stop the entire level dead in it's tracks. During time stop- 90% of enemies can't do anything and the timer does not progress. When you end your time stop ability your character will do a character skill- which is usually a giant blast of damage, though one character doesn't do damage. If you kill a boss their drop will usually put you back into time-stop for free, with the exception of currency rewards. Very quickly it becomes apparent that your goal is to build a character who kills bosses in one hit, to instantly be put back in time stop- so that you can walk over to the next boss and repeat. If you're one shotting you're doing good, and if you notice that you arn't one shotting things anymore you're probably about to lose. Theres an ENTIRE game that you can play without stopping time, but if you're playing that game its almost certainly because you're losing. Let's talk about the rogue-like-ness of this game. This game is not a rogue-like. It's not a Rogue-lite. It's barely even rogue-ish and and times not even rogue-adjacent. This is a tactics game with Diablo-like loot progression. You kill elites, get loot drops, and create sets which persist through runs. the only thing that matters is how high you can jack up your single target character skill damage. Which lets you kill more elites, get more drops, and temp skills per run. Even without using rerolls you will get about the same build every run because theres just a lot of elites to kill and the best skills are just clearly the best skills. I have no clue how to beat any of the bosses or what the bosses even do, I walk up to them and I kill them, If I don't something has gone wrong and they kill me. This continues up till the point where you beat the final boss for the first time. In order to "win the game" you'll now need to use the main character with a really bad set to close out the game. This is pretty not good. It's pretty much the opposite of the entire game you've played up till now and it actually sucks quite a bit. So- just grind up even more numbers to number even harder and kill the bosses without the sets! This seems to be the end game grind which is where I'm at now, and I hope they... you know just cut the ♥♥♥♥ and remove that part. This is obvious padding you make you grind a bit more which the game didn't need at all because it's very repayable without it. Once you're done with that you get to go back to playing the game however you want again! Which I think is pretty great. Finally- i'm just going to mention game balance. This game is NOT balanced. Certain characters are merely better, certain skills are merely better. Every run lets you start with a "run passive" which is based on the char you're playing and theres an obvious best one for each character. Hopefully these get ironed out.

Story: Annoyingly random and inconsistent. Often requires talking to the same NPC multiple times. Choices don't matter. Lots of unskippable dialogue. Currency: Not enough signposting as to what is good and what is not. Currency value icons (like $) are used for multiple different types of the same thing. Currency for the time machine's upgrade system is either not explained or seemingly random. Nothing tracks how much money you get from it. Weapons: They all feel "same," and with 6 weapons total, it feels even moreso like that. Skills that force you to only fire one weapon don't disable the slot buffs for other weapons. Very difficult to compare one to another. Very tedious to determine what to keep and what to recycle. Damage types (poison, etc.) aren't explained very well. Applicable weapons for upgrades aren't explained super well (there's a tiny icon but it changes by color for some reason?). Upgrades in an instance don't usually feel impactful, or force you to otherwise meaninglessly move your weapons around into different slots. Converting temporary weapons to permanent ones is a tedious process that requires prioritizing, storing a few for long term, and then totally forgetting your strategy. Doing it for multiple avatars at once is even more frustrating. Stats: Agility bakes in so many stats while defense seems to do very little. Enemies: Normal mobs feel very same. Elite and Boss mobs have VERY confusing move telegraphs. Sometimes the danger meter fills and then it just launches a slow projectile, while others will just instantly smash you. Some damage is extremely difficult to see, let alone avoid. The goal seems often to be to just deal as much damage as possible and not worry about taking damage (or tech into damage reduction/self-heal), which makes dodging feel bad. Enemy scaling feels wildly disproportionate to my own level once weapons are upgraded, making it difficult to gauge actual difficulty. Very unclear how respawning enemies in a room work. Sometimes it says there will be no more respawns, sometimes, they're just infinite. Music: Randomly changes with no real explanation why. Music themes don't match the zones they're in, especially the home base music, which plays a very melody-forward repetitive song instead of something more relaxed while you're figuring out when to go back in. Home base area: Reasonably well thought-out to be fair, but the NPCs could sign-post their uses better and be combined more. UX/UI: This is the game's weakest, weakest element. It's so hard to organize things. Whenever you do, if you change windows at all, it resets so you lose where your items are. Difficult to compare items. Sorting options are very limited compared to all the ways you can organize gear. HUD is super crowded and unhideable. Buttons for showing inventory, stats, etc., can't be pressed again to close that window. Impossible to look through old upgrades easily to see if a new upgrade is relevant. On upgrade, can't check your inventory or weapons to see how well a particular upgrade will apply. Enemy bullets/attacks are SUPER POORLY telegraphed, to the point where it's almost not worth looking at most of the warning signs. Biggest upgrade would be reworking all damage/indicators/projectiles to be clearly color-coded from enemies and to have the timing of each attack consistent with the indicators. Explanatory text for how something works "for every 1% health lost, gain 1% attack" --but is that multiplicative, additive, and what does "lost" mean? Does "lost" include when you "lose it" when it's from your own skills, taking damage, etc.? No explanations. Some weapons register as dealing no damage. The end DPS detail for each run, when clicking into the "more details," stops showing DPS. Oh man I could go on. The UI/UX is so frustratingly bad that it's the main reason I'm putting this game down. Voice: The character, seemingly totally randomly, says the most generic phrases like "I'm tired," and "Gotta stop time!". Progression: Feels random. Doing the same run a couple times unlocks things with little explanation Quests: can't hide the menu, and there's so many of them that you end up doing anyways just by doing a run, making them pretty pointless. Overall: A C- game. Needs a lot of rework on nearly every element to make this a good game. I enjoyed it for a few hours, but the negatives quickly start making the game more and more frustrating.

[h3]Verdict: Maybe Buy, on Sale.[/h3] Let me preface this by saying, Ascend to Zero is both one of the most frustrating and interesting Roguelites I've played, both in equal measure. It's a very interesting game in concept and at the start - but as you reach lategame, a lot of small issues stack up to make the game rather a chore to play. The game starts off as a fun time stop romp. Until, that is, the fun stops. When you get decent enough gear, the early game just turns into "Press Space to kill boss" then loot their corpse and do it again. This wouldn't be such a big problem, if you could just skip the first few levels like the game gives you the ability to do once you reach Stage 4. But you can't, because without the tech chips from earlier floors, you'll get curb stomped by a level 100,000 raccoon. This gets to the heart of the main problem in Ascend to Zero though - a really fun early game, brought down by one of the most annoying late game experiences I've ever seen. Starting off with gameplay. [b]Gameplay:[/b] If you've ever played Gacha Games - you'll recognise the substat system after a while. It is mostly invisible at the start because substats don't exist on low grade equipment. At the end though? You've got to optimise your build. And substats suck. In gacha games, this is a chore which you're paying to skip. In this game though? You're paying to do it. For some of the Set / Legendary Items, you may need to farm the same easy bosses repeatedly to get an item. These bosses die in 0.1 seconds. However, there's no give up or surrender option on a run. So, you want to farm an item and its substats? You'll basically spend 0.1 of a second actually fighting the boss you wanted to farm, then another 30 seconds waiting for the clock to run down. Then repeat. It's torture. You can also reroll stats, but it's costly. Plus, rerolling doesn't do anything if you don't have the gear in the first place. And, because your character is so reliant on your gear, that leads to the second major problem this game has. [b]Run Variation:[/b] Your equipment has a disproportionate impact on each run, and this is a huge problem for the replayability of this game. Usually, each run in a Roguelite has enough different stuff you can get that changes your playstyle. However, because you need good equipment, and you probably only have 1 or 2 good sets, the difference is minimal between runs. I've been playing as Windborne Spearmaster, and provided you slap enough Attack Speed and decent weapons on them - you turn into a Beyblade. You might only got one good set of equipment though, so want to play a non-Beyblade run? Tough luck, better farm for it. This is made worse by the fact that a lot of the late game equipment provides extra bonuses to ONLY ONE of the six characters. It's great having six classes to choose from, but if I've got a set and legendaries that specifically benefit only one of those characters? I'm going to be playing the character that doesn't slap like a wet noodle. This means you're kind of stuck playing as the one class you happened to drop decent weapons for. Usually in a Roguelike, each run you do something different. But in Ascend to Zero? You're kind of trapped by your kit. Making that even worse is the fact that none of the levels in this game are randomly generated, just the loot and a few special encounters. So, same levels, same character, same build. Kind of sucks the joy out of it. Runs should feel different. But they don't. [b]Scaling:[/b] This is made worse by the ridiculous enemy scaling. If it takes longer than 0.5 seconds to kill a boss? Then you're already behind. Enemies scale so quickly that if you don't get the boss kill EXP chips near the start, the run is over. Enemies and attacks in the later levels also ignore time stop. This wouldn't be so much of a problem if it weren't for the fact that by this point you can end up with upward of 12 time stops and zero ability to actually stop time. Plus, dash just... doesn't dodge attacks. That makes sense, to some degree, as if you play as Windborne Spearmaster you can literally dash forever. However, the unreliability of dash is a major problem in a Bullet Hell Roguelite. There are so many bosses in the game with straight up unavoidable attacks. One boss in the Sewers has an attack that takes up practically the entire room. The only reliable way to dodge its attacks without a working dash is to leave the room faster than a deadbeat dad on the Maury Povich show. [b]Visual Communication:[/b] As you get further into the game, it's clear that the game struggles with visual communication. There's a fight with a boss in Act 2 where the entire screen goes red for an attack then nothing happens. It just launches a few smaller meteor attacks somewhere in that red area. Why? Another enemy in the Desert Stage has an Attack indicator that will fill the room, only for the boss to fire out a wave of tiny pellets that you can kind of just sidestep. It feels underwhelming. [b]Localisation:[/b] The Localisation of this game is... mid at best. It's woefully bad at communicating your abilities - with unviewable substats, shoddy translation, and a lack of information. Frequently, Tech Chips will have opaque descriptions or boost random invisible sub stats. A fair few of them are so bad, reading it feels like a baby projectile word-vomiting alphabet soup at your face. This game is often really bad at communicating with the player and providing information. I'm at the end of the game, and there's still a bunch that the game doesn't tell you. There's also nowhere that explains gear tiers or item grades, which is made a lot more annoying when you find out that Tier 2 (Uncommon) and Tier 5 (Just Beneath Legendary) weapons are nearly the same colour. Combine this with the invisible stat problem, and you've got a lot of confusion. A help cente would be great. So far though, I've only seen two help messages pop up. The first one told me to turn up the difficulty because apparently I'd beaten the Stage 1 boss too fast, and the second one told me that I could reduce the opacity of the damage labels on the screen. This is a feature that I only found because I was dealing so much damage that I couldn't see the enemies through the labels. [b]Conclusion:[/b] Despite the annoying and frustrating endgame, I did enjoy my early experience with this game, and I'm sure that if even a few of these issues were addressed I'd update this review. If this game had shipped in Early Access, I think I would've just given this game a hesitant thumbs up - but as a full release, I can't recommend it. Playing Ascend to Zero is kind of like a death by a thousand cuts. At the start, it's great. At the end, it's just a lot of chores that pad out the runtime. Maybe wait for a big sale and a patch or three before you play.
